summary: Owned units s0067–s0088 are the close of Wang Xizhi’s letter to the Prince of Kuaiji and the start of the separate Xie An letter. No owned unit states a birth, death, age, era name, or reign year. Claim-192 and claim-196 correctly date Yin Hao’s and Xun Xian’s own present command—Wang still treats both as officers who can be sent back to Hefei and Guangling—by a year-precision window AD 352–354. Those endpoints are not guessed from 今/當今; they rest on the letter’s Xu–Luo supply geography and on Jin Shu 8 under Emperor Mu’s Yonghe era: Hao’s northern advance and Xun’s Huaiyin posting in Yonghe 8 (conventional AD 352), and Hao’s dismissal as a commoner in Yonghe 10 month 2 (conventional AD 354). onOrBefore 354 is required because the dismissal itself falls in AD 354; the same window also keeps the competing Jin Shu 80 reading that the letter follows Yao Xiang’s Yonghe 9 defeat. Claim-961 is the same Kuaiji letter’s retrospective citation of Wu Yuan and may share that reception date; empty hints for p027 and p030 correctly keep later reception out of living activity. Claim-211 and claim-232 stay undated, as 時東土饑荒 and the Xie An heading give no year. Claim-963 rightly classifies 尚書僕射 as retrospective heading diction: Xie An received that office in Ningkang 1 (AD 373), long after this Kuaiji-administration letter. Claim-962 is incorrect: 蹈東海 is not a date, and the 352–354 Hao-command window was copied onto a different letter about local grain transport.

itemChecks.event: Yin Hao is still treated as a living commander whom Wang Xizhi asks the prince to send back to hold Hefei.
itemChecks.reason: The dated event belongs to Yin Hao himself: in the Kuaiji-prince letter Wang speaks in the present and asks that Hao be repositioned, so Hao is still an officer, not a later quotation or commemoration. 今/當今 in the letter is deixis, not a reign year; the bounds are contextual. Lower endpoint AD 352: Jin Shu 8, Emperor Mu of Eastern Jin, Yonghe 8, records Hao’s northern expedition to Sikou and the Xu–Luo corridor, matching 今轉運供繼，西輸許洛，北入黃河 and the armies already at Xuchang, Qiao, Liang, and Pengcheng. Conventional Yonghe 8 = AD 352 (year label; the letter does not specify a month/day, so no Julian/Gregorian day conversion is claimed). Upper endpoint AD 354: the same annals, Yonghe 10 month 2, degrade Hao to a commoner; after that Wang could not tell the prince to have Hao 還據合肥. Dismissal falls inside AD 354, so the bound is onOrBefore 354, not before 354. The window also preserves the competing Jin Shu 80 sequence that places this letter after Yao Xiang’s Yonghe 9 (AD 353) defeat and before the Yonghe 10 dismissal. No birth, death, or age for Hao appears in the owned units.

evidence.quote: 令殷浩、荀羨還據合肥、廣陵，許昌、譙郡、梁、彭城諸軍皆還保淮
況今轉運供繼，西輸許洛，北入黃河。
此實當今策之上者。

itemChecks.event: Xun Xian is still treated as a living commander whom Wang Xizhi asks to return and hold Guangling.
itemChecks.reason: The dated event is Xun Xian’s own present command in the same sentence as Hao’s, not a descendant’s act or a later honour. Jin Shu 8, Yonghe 8 month 3 (Emperor Mu, Eastern Jin), posts the Northern Households Lang Xun Xian at Huaiyin, which fits 還據廣陵 and the Huai defensive line. Conventional Yonghe 8 = AD 352 justifies onOrAfter 352 together with the letter’s already-active Xu–Luo transports. The shared upper bound remains Hao’s Yonghe 10 month 2 dismissal in AD 354: after Hao is a commoner the joint present-tense recall collapses, even though Xun himself lived longer. onOrBefore 354 therefore names uncertainty about this letter, not a career span through the dynasty. Xun’s death is not in the owned units and is not required here.

evidence.quote: 令殷浩、荀羨還據合肥、廣陵
況今轉運供繼，西輸許洛，北入黃河。

itemChecks.event: Wang Xizhi opened granaries and repeatedly memorialized during an eastern famine whose year the chapter does not give.
itemChecks.reason: s0083–s0084 narrate 時東土饑荒 and the memorials with no era, reign year, or month. 時 is a sequential ‘at that time’ after the Kuaiji letter, not a calendar date. Leaving the attestation undated is required; inventing a Yonghe year from the neighbouring letter or from Wang’s Kuaiji tenure would turn a boundless 時 into a false year. No birth, death, or age is stated.

evidence.quote: 時東土饑荒，羲之輒開倉振貸。
然朝廷賦役繁重，吳會憂甚，羲之每上疏爭之，事多見從。

itemChecks.event: Xie An is named as the addressee of Wang Xizhi’s letter on local relief and transport.
itemChecks.reason: s0085 only introduces a letter 遺尚書僕射謝安. That is an explicit undated attestation of Xie An as addressee. The heading supplies no year, and the title is separately treated as later diction in claim-963, so this row correctly refuses to turn the heading into a life date or an active year.

evidence.quote: 又遺尚書僕射謝安書曰：

itemChecks.event: Wang Xizhi cites Wu Yuan’s warning as an antiquity applied to the present in the Kuaiji-prince letter.
itemChecks.reason: 伍員之憂不獨在昔 is a retrospective reference: the event dated here is Wang’s citation, not Wu Yuan’s Spring-and-Autumn life. ReceptionType retrospective is the right later-reception category; it does not imply Wu is being given a Jin life date. Because the sentence stands inside the same prince letter as claim-192, the reception may share the AD 352–354 contextual window of that letter (Hao still command-capable; Yonghe 8–10 under Emperor Mu). The phrase is not itself a calendar date; the bounds are those of the letter, not of Wu’s death. Empty living-activity hints for p027 stay consistent with this.

evidence.quote: 常恐伍員之憂不獨在昔，麋鹿之游將不止林藪而已。

itemChecks.event: Wang Xizhi proverbially applies Lu Zhonglian’s stepping into the Eastern Sea to this commandery in the Xie An letter.
itemChecks.reason: s0087 is a different document from the Kuaiji-prince letter: a local-administration letter that begins at s0085. 蹈東海 names Lu Zhonglian’s proverbial act, not a source date, and the letter never mentions Hao, Xun, Hefei, or the Xu–Luo campaign. Copying westernBounds AD 352–354 from Hao’s command window therefore dates the wrong event. The heading 尚書僕射 is later diction (claim-963); 時東土饑荒 still gives no year. The reception itself is real and should be kept as retrospective, but it is undated in this chapter. A later biography may attest an earlier letter, yet it does not license a transferred campaign window. Do not feed this date into p030’s life or hints.

evidence.quote: 又遺尚書僕射謝安書曰：
若不耳，此一郡久以蹈東海矣。
今事之大者未布，漕運是也。

itemChecks.event: The Jin Shu narrator heads Wang’s letter with Xie An’s later title 尚書僕射.
itemChecks.reason: The heading is the historian’s voice, not Xie An acting as Vice Director while Wang writes from Kuaiji. Jin Shu 9, Emperor Xiaowu, Ningkang 1 month 9, first makes 吏部尚書謝安為尚書僕射 after Huan Wen’s death; Jin Shu 79 places 尋為尚書僕射 immediately after 會溫薨. That office is AD 373 reception diction applied to an earlier letter, so kind retrospective-reference / receptionType retrospective is correct. Retrospective does not require proving Xie An dead and is not a life date. Leaving the reception undated avoids inventing a Tang compilation year or treating 373 as Wang’s letter date.

evidence.quote: 又遺尚書僕射謝安書曰：

itemChecks.event: Yin Hao is still a field commander in Wang Xizhi’s present-tense recall to Hefei.
itemChecks.reason: The sole supported personal event for p025 in these units is the living command implied by 令殷浩…還據合肥. The hint AD 352–354 matches that event’s contextual window (Yonghe 8 campaign to Yonghe 10 dismissal) and does not import the Xie An heading or any posthumous reception.

itemChecks.reason: The hint AD 352–354 is the same supported command event as claim-196, not a dynasty-long activity band and not a death date. Xun’s later career and death lie outside these units and are not used as living activity here.

itemChecks.reason: s0081 cites 伍員之憂不獨在昔. That is retrospective reception, which must not feed active-date hints. An empty hint array is required.

itemChecks.reason: s0087 is a retrospective proverb. Empty hints correctly keep that reception out of living activity, including the unsupported 352–354 window on claim-962.

personChecks.reason: Owned evidence for Yin Hao is only the present-tense recall in s0074. That is his own command situation, dated AD 352–354 from Yonghe 8–10 under Emperor Mu, and the hint matches it. No birth, death, or age is present in s0067–s0088, so none was omitted. Context items are empty; the neighbouring undated famine and Xie An letter do not extend or contradict Hao’s command window. Later reception elsewhere is not applied to him.

personChecks.reason: Xun Xian appears only in the same joint recall. His chronology here is that shared living-command window, not a life span and not his later death, which these units never state. Hints stay aligned with claim-196. No omitted age or death in the owned stretch.

The person record has no active hints, and claim-961 keeps the citation as retrospective reception dated to the letter rather than as a Jin life event. The owned units give no birth, death, or age, and this audit must not import a Spring-and-Autumn biography to fill them.

personChecks.reason: Lu Zhonglian appears only in the Xie An letter’s 蹈東海 proverb. Empty hints correctly refuse living activity. The person record itself is coherent; the defective 352–354 reception date is an item error on claim-962, not a life-date or hint on p030. No birth, death, or age is stated in the owned units.

evidence.quote: 此一郡久以蹈東海矣。

findings.problem: Claim-962 dates Wang’s proverbial reception of Lu Zhonglian to AD 352–354 from sourceDate 蹈東海, but that phrase is not a date and the Xie An letter (s0085–s0088) is not the Kuaiji-prince campaign letter that justifies those endpoints.
findings.action: Keep the retrospective event-participation for p030, but remove sourceDate 蹈東海 and the AD 352–354 westernBounds; leave the reception undated or mark it unresolved because this chapter gives no year for the Xie An letter. Do not add an active hint for p030 and do not reuse Hao’s dismissal or Xun’s Huaiyin posting to invent a second endpoint.
